verdict_text: YES. The script loads all three checkpoints (handling the sharded base via its index), asserts identical key sets, asserts bit-equality of every non-MLP tensor against the base before any merging, then computes each of the 48 MLP tensors as `base + 0.4*(ft1-base) + 0.4*(ft2-base)` in float32 against the untouched base dict, copies all other tensors verbatim from the base, asserts `merged == 48` and `len(out) == 114`, and writes `out/T4/model.safetensors`. The regex is anchored with `fullmatch` and matches exactly the three MLP weight names per layer, so the merged/unchanged partition is right.
